structured.approach: I read task.code (BE-05), feat.stories (the STORY-05 and STORY-06 acceptance criteria), ci.py and the existing tests. I ran CI first to get the baseline: 73.2% coverage, with aging.py missing lines 24, 45-58 and 64. Then I added one new file, tests/test_overdue.py, which is the file task.code names for task.components BC-7 and which feat.stories SA-6 allows. It has 21 unittest cases: one or more for each of AC-05.1 to AC-05.10 and AC-06.1 to AC-06.4, plus checks that the existing functions still behave as before (T-11), including the bucket_for "1-30" branch flagged in CQ-BE-3. All data is synthetic SYN-INV-*. Day counts are made exact by setting each due date to as_of minus a fixed number of days. I reran CI until it passed (it passed on the first run) and wrote task.unit_tests.md with the mapping from each criterion to its test, the CI results before and after, and open questions. I did not use a verifier subagent: the output is short, and every number in it comes straight from the two CI runs or the inputs.

claims.text: Before this step CI ran 3 tests with total coverage 73.2; aging.py was at 71% with lines 24, 45-58 and 64 missing, so CI did not pass
After adding tests/test_overdue.py, CI ran 24 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors, total line coverage 100.0, no static issues, and passed is true
The new test file is tests/test_overdue.py, the file task.components BC-7 plans; feat.stories SA-6 allows a lane to add new test files
Tests check that exactly 30 days past due is not listed and that 31 days is listed with calendar days (AC-05.1, AC-05.2, lesson L-007)

Tests check that paid and not-yet-due invoices are not listed, the five row keys, the sort by days descending then id ascending as text, 'unknown' risk, Decimal('980.5') quantised to 980.50, no call to bucket_for, and KeyError for a missing vendor (AC-05.3 to AC-05.10)
Tests check the CT-1 JSON: same order, key order, days as an int, amount as a two-decimal string such as 1250.00, '[]' for no rows, and no date field (AC-06.1 to AC-06.4)
The bucket_for 'return "1-30"' branch that task.code reported as uncovered (CQ-BE-3) is now covered by bucket_for(1) and bucket_for(29); bucket_for(30) still returns '31-60'
Only tests/test_overdue.py was added in this step; tests/test_aging.py and the code outside tests/ are unchanged

open_questions: UQ-BE-1 (non-blocking, tied to TQ-9): AC-05.10 says a missing vendor raises KeyError, but the code reads vendor only for listed (overdue) invoices, so a paid, not-yet-due or exactly-30-days invoice with no vendor raises nothing. Should a missing vendor raise for every invoice?
Carried unchanged (non-blocking): TQ-1, TQ-3, TQ-9, PQ-2. The tests pin the current interim designs and must change if an answer changes a [Pending] criterion.
structured.summary: CI now passes. I added tests/test_overdue.py with 21 unit tests covering STORY-05 overdue_with_risk (AC-05.1 to AC-05.10), STORY-06 overdue_rows_to_json (AC-06.1 to AC-06.4), and checks that the existing aging functions behave as before. CI ran 24 tests with 0 failures and 0 errors, at 100.0% line coverage (up from 73.2; the gate is 90) and with no static issues. The new tests also cover the bucket_for "1-30" branch (CQ-BE-3). The results are in task.unit_tests.md. One question remains open and does not block anything: whether a missing vendor should raise KeyError for invoices that are not listed (UQ-BE-1).

tool_input.command: cat ci.py && ls tests && git status --short && /usr/bin/python3 ci.py 2>&1 | tail -15
tool_input.description: Show CI script, test files, and run CI baseline
